{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our table built a fish: nose, two body lines splitting round the head, and a forked tail. My part was the lower tail stroke, which I laid once the bottom body line reached the junction. I also inspected the nose split. By my trace, all 98 standing dominoes were connected to the start. I don't know yet how it read once it fell. We used under half our dominoes, and the pad had an 'eye' label that we never built. A fish outline is recognizable, but an eye or a fin would have added a margin of safety. I should have raised that while we had time.

Execution: I did my stroke cleanly and checked the nose joint and my tail fin by inspection and by tracing the start. I stayed away from the tail joint after Priya flagged it, which avoided a bump risk. My status reports to you were accurate, and I only said things I had checked.

Collaboration: Priya and Maya both started on the pad, and we settled it quickly. I accepted Priya's sketch and her role assignments instead of arguing over whose plan it was. I stuck to my stroke and kept out of Tom's and Maya's areas. I offered to restand anything that got bumped. I'd also say I mostly echoed the group in the quiet stretch and didn't add much.

Leadership: Priya led this one. My default is to set the plan, but here I backed her, which was the right call because two competing plans would have cost time. I confirmed the assignments and kept you informed. Where I could have done more was in using the spare time and dominoes to propose a low-risk improvement, such as an eye. I'd do that next time."}
